messages:
anya: quick status: onboarding bench for orenda13b (int4) shows surprising latency bump and sporadic OOMs on long-gen workloads.
marc: saw that in perf dashboard. latency p50 went from 120ms -> 220ms on the canary pool?
priya: i have the benchmark CSV, attaching summary: avg p50=210ms, p95=1.1s, avg tokens/sec per GPU down 30%. quality (embedding-sim) stable ~0.998 vs fp16 baseline.
jin: so accuracy fine but perf is worse; this screams memory-fragmentation/kv cache churn with int4 kernels. any logs?
anya: pulled a pod log, snippet: 
```
2026-03-22T09:12:11Z INFO  request id=abc gen_tokens=1024 route=orenda13b-int4
2026-03-22T09:12:11Z WARN  kv_cache: slot_growth=+8 total_slots=512
2026-03-22T09:12:11Z ERROR oom: alloc failed for attention_kv shm=1048576000
```
leo: pattern: medium-long gens + default batch=4 + prefetch=2 -> heavy tail of slot allocations. int4 reduces per-tensor size but increases slot count because of more aggressive prefetching.
sara: experiment idea: two forks — safety-first (conservative defaults) and perf-first (batching+kv tuning).
priya: conservative defaults patch I ran locally: max_new_tokens=512, prefetch_window=1, batch_size=2, soft_evict=true. result: p50=140ms p95=420ms, no OOMs in 1h smoke.
marc: great. what's the perf-first plan?
jin: perf-first: keep batch_size=4, set adaptive_prefetch: dynamic reduce prefetch when free_slots<0.2, and enable slot_compactor every 5m. hope to retain throughput while bounding fragmentation.
anya: we tried perf-first for 30m: throughput improved 12% but we saw 3 OOMs in 30m during randomized long-gen replay. not safe for rollout.
leo: other lever: reduce kv_cache pre-allocation granularity (smaller slot size) — trades kernel alignment. need infra sign-off.
sara: also noticed small quality drift for int4 under some prompts in long context: embedding-sim drop to 0.985 in 0.05% of cases. we should gate that.
priya: propose rollout plan: 1) apply conservative defaults to canary pool (route-level) 2) smoke 1h with 200 randomized long-gen replays and 100 eval prompts (threshold: <0.5% quality delta, no OOMs) 3) if pass, ramp to 10% traffic with slowstart and nvml snapshots.
marc: add routing fallback: for requests where requested max_new_tokens > 1024 route to orenda13b-int8 automatically. keep this rule in case long gens appear.
anya: ops-bot: run deploy job?
ops-bot: deploybot: patch deploy queued by priya — job #3819. will run canary for 60m and collect smoke evals. :gear:
jin: diagnostics to capture: nvml snapshots, jemalloc stats, and our slot-usage histogram every 30s. add `--mem-histogram` to the smoke runner.
leo: after deploy, add a quick regression test: 500 synthetic conversation turns (mixed lengths) to detect fragmentation trends. run compactor interval to 300s during canary.
sara: i'll write a short eval harness that compares fp16 vs int4 outputs for our long-context smoke set and report embedding-sim and token-mismatch counts. will post results in thread.
priya: i'll open PR with config and the routing fallback. linking perf dashboards and logs in PR.
anya: thanks — i'll keep the canary on hold until PR lands, then kick job #3819. if we see >2 OOMs in 60m auto-rollback.
marc: once stable, add checklist note to onboarding doc: "int4: conservative prefetch, max_new_tokens <=512, require smoke evals vs fp16 on long-ctx set".
anya: noted. updating incident board with P0 -> P2 depending on regression outcome.
sara: FYI — small spike in p95 correlated with slot_compactor disabled on one node. compactor fixes fragmentation quickly, so ensure compactor enabled cluster-wide.
jin: for longer term: investigate kernel scheduling (coalesce small allocations) and slot reuse heuristics. open R&D ticket.
anya: great. will follow up with results after canary. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
